title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
technique: IO-aware tiled exact attention fusing softmax into one kernel, recomputation in backward, minimizing HBM reads/writes

optimized_metrics.evidence: An important question is whether making attention faster and more memory-efficient can help Transformer models address their runtime and memory challenges for long sequences.
One of our goals is to not store O(N^2) intermediate values for the backward pass.
Our goal is to reduce the amount of HBM accesses (to sub-quadratic in N).
IO-aware exact attention algorithm (exactness: no approximation, unlike approximate attention that trades off model quality)

headline_claim.text: FlashAttention trains Transformers faster than existing baselines: 15% end-to-end wall-clock speedup on BERT-large (seq. length 512) compared to the MLPerf 1.1 training speed record, 3× speedup on GPT-2 (seq. length 1K), and 2.4× speedup on long-range arena (seq. length 1K-4K).

reported_metrics.where: Fig 3 left, Fig 8 (attention runtime fwd+bwd, fwd only on T4)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Approximate attention methods have attempted to address this problem by trading off model quality to reduce the compute complexity, but often do not achieve wall-clock speedup.
metric_definitions.notes: Speedup = runtime ratio vs PyTorch/other attention; no serving latency or throughput metric defined

load_regime: fixed batch size / sequence-length sweep (kernel microbenchmarks; training runs)
tradeoff_acknowledged: Backward pass has more FLOPs than standard attention due to recomputation, but fewer HBM accesses, so is faster; on T4 less speedup due to smaller SRAM; for seq>1K some approximate methods are faster.
workloads: training and attention microbenchmarks; no serving workload
extractor_notes: Kernel-level paper; design targets kernel runtime (HBM IO) and memory, not end-to-end serving metrics. Evaluated mostly on TRAINING; inference only appears as a forward-only speedup on T4. Largely out of serving scope (training-focused); recorded as kernel baseline. No TTFT/throughput/latency in serving sense.
